A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original VS/AVI verification, correction, ablation and runtime experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds natural-chain veracity measurements, broader correlations, runtime measurements and model-size experiments.

M1.justification: The latent-variable model, greedy initialization, Metropolis search, annealing and AVI training procedure remain unchanged. Block updates, categorical labels and Self-Refine integration already appear in v2. The new caching discussion does not establish an implemented procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions already use PRONTOQA, GSM8K and COMMONSENSEQA, including naturally generated PRONTOQA/COMMONSENSEQA chains and three-class PRONTOQA. The added measurements and model configurations extend analysis within this existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Recursive, Many2Many, Voting and CoT remain in Table 1; existing search and correction comparisons also retain their comparators. New experiments use the existing Many2Many baseline. Newly cited process reward models are discussed but not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds direct natural-error evaluation against GPT-4.1 pseudo-labels on 1,000 test samples per task, Qwen3-1.7B/14B evaluations, and a runtime protocol using 100 Metropolis iterations across 3-11 reasoning steps. Appendix C.2 also replaces separate 5,000-PRONTOQA and 10,000-COMMONSENSEQA training accounts with a common 10,000-triple description. Its dataset allocation and whether retained experiments were rerun are unspecified.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds direct verification analysis for naturally occurring errors, broadens likelihood-veracity correlation analysis from two Qwen models on PRONTOQA to four models on two datasets, and adds model-size sensitivity and runtime scaling studies. Existing corruption-pattern, search-hyperparameter, block-update and categorical analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 11 specifies averaging runtime measurements over five independent runs, whereas v2's runtime study does not specify independent repetitions. No dispersion is supplied for these new timings. Existing five-run/seed and standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged; increased repetitions for retained experiments are not established.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports natural-chain Hamming similarity of 0.92 versus 0.74 for VS versus Many2Many on PRONTOQA, and 0.86 versus 0.59 on COMMONSENSEQA. Tables 10-12 add six correlation values, runtime measurements of 7.33-13.09 seconds, and 1.7B/14B model results across three benchmarks. Previously reported numerical entries and figure data are retained; these additions do not demonstrate performance changes between versions under fixed settings.

T1.justification: Appendix C.6 adds asymptotic cost expressions for repeated likelihood scoring, prefix caching and an expected suffix-length reduction. The latent-variable definitions, posterior equations, proxy reward and Metropolis mathematics in Section 2 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and central conclusion retain the claims about VS, answer-independent AVI, verification accuracy and usefulness as correction feedback. Added experiments support these existing claims. EM/PRM training is suggested as a future application.

C2.justification: Sections 4.4 and C.2 newly interpret smaller downstream answer gains than verification gains as evidence of a reasoning/refinement bottleneck. Appendix C.6 qualifies runtime advantages as search iterations increase, and the conclusion suggests EM and PRM training applications. Existing limitations concerning synthetic errors remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a source-code link in Section 4 and documents teacher-forced likelihood scoring, possible caching optimizations, and hardware and iteration details for the new timing study. Appendix A's implementation information is unchanged. The merged natural-chain correction account no longer explicitly specifies its decoding temperature, previously T=0.01.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds a focused comparison with process reward models, distinguishing step correctness from outcome-trained value or advantage. It also discusses prompt fragility and acknowledges prior verification/refinement decomposition. Six references are added, while the broader positioning alongside self-correction and search remains.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose revisions, splits Appendix C.1 into synthetic and natural-error subsections, and merges v2's C.2-C.3 correction discussions. It updates publication headers and adds an LLM-usage disclosure. Most main-text exposition and Appendices A-B remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5, 11 and 12 and expands/restructures v2's correlation Table 9 into Table 10. Existing material undergoes local reflow and relocation, including Figure 3. All five figures retain their content, and the overall visual template remains stable.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens a specific evidential gap: v2 assessed naturally occurring errors indirectly through answer correction, while new Table 5 directly measures veracity against GPT-4.1 pseudo-labels. Broader correlation and model-size checks, cost analysis, code-access information and clearer discussion of downstream bottlenecks improve support and clarity. These gains remain bounded by reliance on model-generated reference labels and ambiguity introduced by the merged AVI training description.
